source.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares convolutional and locally connected students and measures generalization error under varied spatial correlations, kernel sizes, and learning-rate choices in an exactly analyzed teacher–student model. This conceptually bears on architecture and generalization, but does not test natural-label image classification or random-label memorization.
record.gate_note: Own results include error trajectories and noise floors under architecture, locality, and correlation conditions. The paper's cited empirical CNN/FCN comparisons are prior work and are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures learning dynamics and population regression error for convolutional versus locally connected students on synthetic Gaussian inputs. It does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers, as V3 requires, or test any other version. Its discussion of CNN–FCN comparisons cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The exact P-fold speedup assumes uncorrelated positions and matched position-symmetric initial conditions in the high-dimensional dynamics. The locality sample-complexity result is numerical. Under spatial correlations and label noise, LCNs have lower asymptotic error at the same small learning rate, whereas separately optimized constant learning rates allow CNNs to win at long training horizons.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical teacher–student regression model with Gaussian inputs and online SGD; compares CNN and LCN students through high-dimensional ODEs, not standard image-classification networks trained on natural labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on spatial correlation c, student kernel size ks relative to teacher kt, training horizon, and whether learning rates are held fixed or optimized separately. The c = 0 time-rescaling result holds for erf and ReLU; it fails at c = 0.5.

fits_no_version.finding: For independent positions and matched position-symmetric initial conditions, the CNN follows the LCN's regression-error trajectory with P times fewer SGD steps; spatial correlations break this identity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight sharing can accelerate online teacher–student learning by an exact factor determined by the number of positions, with the advantage depending on input correlations.

fits_no_version.finding: Matching teacher locality requires O(D) samples for specialization; larger tested kernels require O(D log D), with the plateau persisting under correlated inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Excess receptive-field size can increase teacher-recovery sample complexity through a symmetry-induced learning plateau.

fits_no_version.finding: At the same small constant learning rate under label noise, the CNN noise floor increases with spatial correlation while the LCN floor stays constant; ReLU simulations show the same qualitative pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spatial correlations can make shared-weight regression students less robust to label noise than otherwise matched locally connected students.

fits_no_version.finding: With constant learning rates optimized separately at each horizon, LCNs win at short horizons with strong correlations and CNNs win at long horizons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization-error ranking of shared and unshared local architectures can depend on training horizon and architecture-specific learning-rate tuning.

record.problems: The study uses a simplified synthetic Gaussian teacher–student regression setup and one-pass online SGD. It does not test classification, natural-image data, fully connected networks, or finite-dataset memorization. Some comparisons are numerical ODE integrations or plots; several precise values are not stated in text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted. Cited prior-work comparisons in Section 1.1 were excluded because they are not results from this study.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out classification performance.
Test error as hidden-layer width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
CNN versus FCN image-classification error, the contribution of local connectivity to that difference, learned sparse local connections, and initialization from trained CNNs.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization and dependence on tuning or weight-decay choices.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects, small-data failures, excessive dropout, and removal alongside weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions because the measurements do not instantiate those versions; this does not dispute the reported regression results. The record's V3 limits_scope labels should be removed.

versions.untested_parts: Natural labels versus random labels, memorization capacity, and held-out classification accuracy are not tested.
No one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep beyond interpolation is tested.
No fully connected student is tested; inputs are synthetic Gaussian regression data, not image-classification benchmarks; local connectivity is compared with weight sharing.
No adaptive optimizer comparison is tested.
No minibatch-size or fixed-epoch comparison is tested; training is online SGD.
Dropout and weight decay are not tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization measure is evaluated.
No training-example removal or memorized-example analysis is conducted.

rows.subject: CNN student

rows.operation_detail: Online SGD training; generalization error compared with LCN after rescaling LCN time by P.
rows.baseline: LCN at training time Pα; trajectories coincide after time rescaling by P
rows.value: CNN trajectory εg(α); coincides with rescaled LCN trajectory
rows.note: The plotted SGD simulations and ODE curves are described as coinciding after the LCN time rescaling. This is a synthetic teacher–student regression setup, not a comparison with fully connected image classifiers.
rows.check: The reported time-rescaled equality concerns CNN versus LCN regression dynamics, not the CNN–FCN image-classification advantage in V3.

rows.value: LCN converges faster than CNN even without rescaling time
rows.note: The text explicitly says the rescaling fails at c > 0 and that the LCN converges faster in this displayed condition. The version's broad CNN-versus-fully-connected image-classification claim is outside this synthetic comparison.
rows.check: Faster LCN convergence at c = 0.5 does not measure V3's CNN–FCN comparison.

rows.subject: CNN student
rows.operation_detail: Compare asymptotic generalization error under label noise across spatial correlations at fixed small learning rate.
rows.baseline: LCN noise floor at the same learning rate: ησ²P/(π√(1 + 2T)) + O(η²), independent of c
rows.value: ησ²/π [P/√(1 + 2T) + P(P − 1)c/√((1 + T)² − T²c²)] + O(η²); grows with c
rows.note: At c = 0 the CNN and LCN noise floors coincide; for c > 0, the CNN floor grows with c and the LCN floor stays independent of c. The result is for regression with label noise.
rows.check: The formula measures a CNN regression noise floor relative to an LCN, not a fully connected image classifier.

rows.subject: LCN student
rows.operation_detail: Compare asymptotic generalization error under label noise across spatial correlations at fixed small learning rate.
rows.baseline: CNN noise floor at c = 0; both floors coincide there
rows.value: ησ²P/(π√(1 + 2T)) + O(η²), independent of c and lower than CNN for c > 0 at the same learning rate
rows.note: The LCN is less affected by spatial correlations in the stated asymptotic noisy-regression setting.
rows.check: The LCN's lower regression noise floor for c > 0 does not challenge V3 because its required FCN comparator is absent.
